tagging_basis: OCR H432 numbered specification sections (lettered learning outcomes as evidence)

units.label: 1(a)(i)
units.summary: Calculate the relative atomic mass of titanium from isotope abundances to two decimal places.

units.label: 1(a)(ii)
units.summary: Complete the electron configuration of a titanium atom.

units.label: 1(a)(iii)
units.summary: Give the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons in 48Ti2+.

units.label: 1(b)(i)
units.summary: Give the systematic name of TiO2 using a Roman numeral.

units.label: 1(b)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the minimum mass of sodium needed to make 1.00 kg of titanium at a given percentage yield.

units.label: 1(b)(iii)
units.summary: Suggest how to separate titanium from sodium chloride at room temperature and explain why.

units.label: 2(a)(i)
units.summary: Write the equation for calcium with water and predict one observation.

units.label: 2(a)(ii)
units.summary: Suggest one observation difference between barium and calcium reacting with water.

units.label: 2(b)(i)
units.summary: Write an equation with state symbols for formation of barium sulfate.

units.label: 2(b)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the percentage by mass of NaCl in a mixture from the mass of barium sulfate precipitate.
units.difficulty_basis: Multi-step mass calculation in an unfamiliar context

units.label: 2(b)(iii)
units.summary: Explain whether using excess silver nitrate would allow determination of NaCl percentage.

units.label: 2(c)(i)
units.summary: Complete a table giving the lattice type for four substances from melting point and conductivity data.
units.difficulty_basis: Applying structure and bonding to data

units.label: 2(c)(ii)
units.summary: Explain the melting point of MgS versus PCl3 and conductivity of aluminium versus silicon.

units.label: 3(a)
units.summary: Explain why chlorine is more reactive than iodine and calculate the volume of seawater needed for 1.00 tonne of iodine.
units.difficulty_basis: Six mark combined explanation and unfamiliar multi-step calculation

units.label: 3(b)
units.summary: State what is meant by disproportionation and use oxidation numbers in the formation of bleaching powder.

units.label: 3(c)
units.summary: Outline the mechanism for alkaline hydrolysis of 2-bromopropane and name it.
units.difficulty_basis: Standard mechanism with a secondary haloalkane

units.label: 3(d)(i)
units.summary: Give the formula and colour of the silver halide precipitates for two haloalkanes.

units.label: 3(d)(ii)
units.summary: Predict which precipitate forms first and explain the rate difference in hydrolysis.

units.label: 4(a)
units.summary: Explain the term enthalpy change of combustion.

units.label: 4(b)(i)
units.summary: Calculate the percentage uncertainty in a temperature change from a thermometer uncertainty.

units.label: 4(b)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the enthalpy change of combustion of butan-1-ol, explain the difference from the data book value and suggest improvements.
units.difficulty_basis: Six mark calculation plus evaluation of design

units.label: 4(b)(iii)
units.summary: Calculate the mass of butan-1-ol giving the same temperature rise with less water.
units.difficulty_basis: Reasoning with proportionality in a modified experiment

units.label: 4(c)(i)
units.summary: Use the enthalpy of combustion and average bond enthalpies to find the C=O bond enthalpy.

units.label: 4(c)(ii)
units.summary: Explain why the enthalpy of combustion of methoxymethane differs from ethanol in terms of bonds broken and formed.

units.label: 5(a)(i)
units.summary: Give the systematic name of a branched secondary alcohol.

units.label: 5(a)(ii)
units.summary: Write the equation for dehydration of alcohol A to the alkene that has no E/Z isomers.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs isomer reasoning to select product

units.label: 5(a)(iii)
units.summary: Use CIP priority rules to explain why alkene B is the Z isomer.

units.label: 5(b)(i)
units.summary: Draw two repeat units of an addition polymer and suggest why it is soluble in water.
units.difficulty_basis: Polymer drawing plus hydrogen bonding link

units.label: 5(b)(ii)
units.summary: Outline two useful ways of processing waste hydrocarbon polymers instead of landfill.
